fullPassage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light — a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless — and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective — "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.

(A) Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective <u>property</u> of things.
(B) The old house and the wide land around it are now my family's <u>property</u>, left to us by my grandfather.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 property의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 재산/소유물 — (B) 속성/특성: (A)의 property는 색의 '속성/특성'이지 재산이 아님
✅ ② (A) 속성/특성 — (B) 재산/소유물: (A)는 'an objective property of things(사물의 객관적 속성)', (B)는 'my family's property(가족의 재산)'로 다의어의 두 쓰임을 올바르게 연결 ←정답
❌ ③ (A) 속성 — (B) 예의: (B)의 property는 예의가 아닌 '재산'
❌ ④ (A) 부동산 — (B) 속성: (A)는 부동산이 아닌 '속성'
det.tip: property: ① (명사) 속성/특성 ② (명사) 재산/소유물

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to explain or understand the meaning of something"

det.analysis:
❌ ① reflect: reflect(반사하다)는 빛·소리를 되돌려 보내는 것으로 정의와 무관
❌ ② inhabit: inhabit(깃들다/거주하다)은 의미를 해석하는 것과 다름
✅ ③ interpret: interpret(해석하다)은 '무언가의 의미를 설명하거나 이해하다'라는 영영 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ bounce: bounce(튕기다)는 해석과 무관
det.tip: interpret = 해석하다 (interpreted by the brain)

questions.passage: They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light — a __________ (green) that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 관사 a 뒤에 명사가 필요하므로 형용사 green을 명사 greenness로 바꾼다
det.analysis: 'a ___ that is just as real as the leaves'에서 관사 a 뒤에 명사가 와야 하며, 뒤의 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 되어야 한다. 형용사 green을 명사형으로 바꾸면 greenness(녹색임/녹색의 성질)가 된다. green → greenness
det.tip: 형용사 green → 명사 greenness (관사 a 뒤에는 명사)

questions.passage: Color is objective and subjective — "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is __________ (register) by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 빛이 '감지되는' 수동이므로 be동사 is 뒤에 과거분사 registered
det.analysis: 'light from the world is ___ by the eyes'에서 빛이 눈에 의해 감지되는 수동태(be + p.p.)가 필요하다. 뒤의 interpreted(과거분사)와 and로 병렬되므로 과거분사 registered가 적절하다. register → registered
det.tip: 수동태 병렬: is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain

questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that __________ them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light — a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless — and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective — "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: bounces off=~에서 튕겨 나오다 — 사물에서 튕겨 나오는 빛의 속성이라는 맥락
det.analysis:
✅ ① bounces off: 원문 일치. 'the light that ___ them'에서 사물에서 튕겨 나오는(bounces off) 빛이라는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② settles on(~에 내려앉다): 빛이 사물에서 '튕겨 나온다'는 맥락과 다름
❌ ③ comes from(~에서 오다): 반사되어 나온다는 구체적 의미와 어긋남
❌ ④ hides behind(~뒤에 숨다): 빛이 튕겨 나온다는 맥락과 반대
det.tip: the light that bounces off them — 사물에서 튕겨 나오는 빛

questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light — a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless — and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, __________, correct. Color is objective and subjective — "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: in a way=어떤 면에서는 — 두 입장 모두 어떤 면에서는 옳다는 맥락
det.analysis:
❌ ① by no means(결코 ~아닌): 두 입장이 '옳다'는 맥락과 반대
❌ ② for sure(확실히): 뒤이어 '객관적이면서 주관적'이라는 절충이 오므로 단정은 부적절
❌ ③ at all(전혀): 부정문에 쓰이는 표현으로 맥락과 불일치
✅ ④ in a way: 원문 일치. 'Both positions are, ___, correct'에서 두 입장 모두 '어떤 면에서는(in a way)' 옳다는 절충의 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: Both positions are, in a way, correct — 두 입장 모두 어떤 면에서는 옳다
